label: accepted

evidence.V1: Arrow-pointed board on a capped post reads instantly in front, three-quarter and silhouette; top view still reads as board + post cap; directional board is asymmetric by design (symmetric null, A15 pass).
evidence.V2: Clear hierarchy: big arrow board + post, medium inset face panel and gold caps, small raised cross icon and two ink bolts.
evidence.V3: Chunky stylised proportions: thick framed board, oversized gold mushroom caps top and bottom, board centred on the post (front view board spans ~130-380 px around post at ~252).
evidence.V4: Consistent ~0.045-stud chamfers on frame, inset face, arrow tip corners, cross arms and caps all catch a highlight in studio close-ups.
evidence.V5: Close-ups clean: no seams, pinches or z-fighting on board edge, icon or face; seats all gap 0 with small intended penetrations; cap rim slightly polygonal in outline but shading smooth.
evidence.V6: Disciplined: one wood hue in three values (dark frame/post, mid board, light face) + gold accent + ink bolts; teal/walnut colourways keep the same structure.
evidence.V7: 1108 tris vs medium target 2000 (ceiling 4000): well under target.
evidence.V8: Matches kit: single white LF_VertexColor material, gold accent, ink dark, chamfer size and smooth shading indistinguishable from the kit sign anchor.
evidence.V9: Studio line correct: Anchored, CollisionFidelity Box, CanTouch off, MeshPart.Color white for vertex colours, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre.

top_fixes: Raise segment count on the post caps so the dome rim outline is less polygonal in close-up
Consider a matching bolt pair near the arrow end or a subtle grain groove so the right half of the board carries some small detail
Use an icon that reinforces direction (arrow/chevron) or leave the face for a SurfaceGui, since the cross reads as a health marker
